title: Removing QRACM from QFT Linear Key-Recovery Attacks
summary: Q1 QFT-based linear key-recovery attacks require large QRACM for efficient correlation-state construction; removing this memory requirement remains open.

formal_statement.body: In the Q1 model of QFT-based linear key-recovery attacks, efficiently constructing the correlation states requires querying attack data in superposition, which requires a large QRACM resource: quantum-accessible classical memory. The unresolved problem is whether this QRACM memory requirement can be removed. The question is motivated by the offline-Simon algorithm, where quantum queries made during each Grover iterate are instead performed once and reused; here, however, the queries are embedded in quantum amplitude amplification, making analogous query reuse more challenging.

scope.domain: Quantum linear cryptanalysis and the memory complexity of QFT-based key-recovery attacks.
assumptions: The attacks are considered in the Q1 model.
parameters: QRACM memory — quantum-accessible classical memory enabling superposition queries to attack data
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the QRACM memory requirement can be removed from these attacks.

citations.label: Quantum Linear Key-recovery Attacks Using the QFT

progress.summary: The source explicitly poses removal of the QRACM requirement as an important question. It cites offline-Simon-style query reuse as motivation while noting that queries embedded in amplitude amplification make an analogous approach more challenging.
